clue.text: Novice morphed into a penetrating examiner

indicators.note: penetrating means going into, so the shuffled letters sit inside the examiner's word

parts.note: a prober is one who examines or investigates

indicators.note: morphed means changed shape, so the letters of 'into a' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trainee turns into a sharp-eyed inspector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novice morphed' reads as one phrase, but 'morphed' acts on 'into a' (giving ATION), and 'penetrating' sets that within the examiner.
explanation.definitionFit: A probationer is a newcomer on trial in a job, hence a novice.

clue.text: Lover for Parisian entertaining alpha male?

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the French word contains the other pieces

parts.note: pour is French for 'for'
A is alpha in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's lover is entertaining the top dog of the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alpha male' looks like one idea, but it splits into alpha and male, and 'entertaining' sets both within the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramour is an illicit sweetheart, a synonym for lover.

clue.text: Maybe spleen is beginning to motivate creature

parts.note: the spleen is an example of an organ, hence 'Maybe'

indicators.note: beginning to signals taking just the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Bad temper is what starts a creature moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spleen' looks like ill humour, but here it is the body part; 'beginning to' gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: Any living creature is an organism, a living thing.

clue.text: Chain in patrician descent not complete

indicators.note: in signals that the letters are found inside the following words
not complete tells us the hidden run uses only part of the words, not all of them

explanation.surface: A noble lineage that has gaps in it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are a mountain chain running down South America.

clue.text: Commandeer one penny bank invests

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: invests here means is put into, so the penny goes inside the bank

parts.note: a mound is a raised bank of earth

explanation.surface: Seizing a single coin that the bank puts its money in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money, but it is a bank of earth, MOUND.
explanation.definitionFit: To impound property is to seize or confiscate it officially, to commandeer it.

clue.text: Fugitive losing head in New York convent

indicators.note: in places the shortened word between the letters for the American city
losing head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a runner is someone on the run, a fugitive

explanation.surface: A fugitive hides out in a New York convent.
explanation.definitionFit: A nunnery is a house where nuns live, i.e. a convent.

clue.text: Monied speculator acquiring East German house

indicators.note: acquiring means taking in, so the compass letter goes inside the wealthy word

parts.note: monied means wealthy, rich
a stag is a stock-market speculator who buys new shares to sell quickly

explanation.surface: A wealthy investor buys up property in the east.
explanation.walkthrough: A STAG is City slang for one who applies for new share issues to sell them on at a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reichstag is the building housing Germany's parliament, so a German house of legislators.

clue.text: Obscure hawk avoiding lake

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out, so the lake letter is removed

parts.note: to hawk goods is to sell them; flog is British slang for selling

explanation.surface: An obscure bird of prey steering clear of a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hawk' is a verb, to peddle; FLOG is British slang for sell.
explanation.definitionFit: To fog something is to blur or cloud it, to make it obscure.

clue.text: Leaves father and daughter among statisticians

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: among means placed inside, so the daughter's letter sits within the statisticians

parts.note: ONS is the UK's Office for National Statistics

explanation.surface: A dad and his girl leave a group of number crunchers.
explanation.walkthrough: ONS is the Office for National Statistics, the UK's official statistics body.
explanation.definitionFit: Fronds are the large divided leaves of ferns and palms.

clue.text: Environmentalists putting on these vegetables

definitions.meaning: members of ecological parties are known by this colour
in golf, putting is done on the smooth lawns around the holes
leafy vegetables such as cabbage and kale go by this name

explanation.surface: Eco-campaigners serving up a side of veg.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: the middle one is golf, where the putting is done on smooth turf.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecologists in politics, golf's putting surfaces and leafy veg all share the same colour-based name.

clue.text: Boss on tabloid had a meltdown?

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the editor comes behind the paper

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a tabloid paper
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor loses it over the tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Raged means flew into a fury, which is what a metaphorical meltdown is.

clue.text: God one wearing the specified tights

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

indicators.note: wearing here means the outer word is put on, so it wraps around the single letter

parts.note: those points to the specific things mentioned
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A god is pulling on a particular pair of tights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' wraps THOSE around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantihose is the British spelling of pantyhose, women's sheer tights.

clue.text: Dressing thrown at us going into chopped lamb?

indicators.note: going into means the shuffled letters are put inside the meat word

parts.note: mince is chopped-up meat, here lamb

indicators.note: thrown means tossed about, so the letters of 'at us' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sauce flung at us lands on the minced lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' shuffles 'at us' and 'going into' sets that within the chopped lamb; the question mark admits the lamb is only one kind of mince.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint sauce is a sharp condiment traditionally served as a dressing with roast lamb.

clue.text: Tricked where subatomic particle has no radius

indicators.note: has no means the following letter is missing from the particle

parts.note: a hadron is a subatomic particle such as a proton
R is the abbreviation for radius in geometry

explanation.surface: A physicist is fooled by a particle lacking a dimension.
explanation.definitionFit: To have someone on is a British idiom for teasing or fooling them.

clue.text: Blue Berets report not reliable

parts.note: United Nations peacekeepers wear blue berets
a report is a loud noise, a sound

explanation.surface: A dispatch from peacekeepers can't be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like a dispatch, but it is a bang.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsound reasoning is flawed and so cannot be relied on.

clue.text: In good order until put out

parts.note: up to means until, as in 'up to now'
to snuff a candle is to put it out

explanation.surface: Things were tidy until someone put out the light.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: up to snuff means meeting the required standard, in good condition.

clue.text: Himalayan legend still current

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not yet'
I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: A mountain myth that still has currency today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like an adjective meaning present-day, but it is electric current, I.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti, or abominable snowman, is a creature of Himalayan folklore.

clue.text: City airport redeveloped covers Spain

indicators.note: covers means surrounds, so the rearranged letters go around the country letter
redeveloped means rebuilt into a new form, so the letters of airport are rearranged

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A rebuilt airport is serving routes to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redeveloped' rearranges AIRPORT; 'covers' puts those letters around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is a city, the administrative capital of South Africa.

clue.text: Church charged by female over evil material

indicators.note: charged by means filled with, so the church letters hold the other pieces

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: over means placed above in a down answer, so the bird comes first

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
ill can mean evil or harm, as in 'speak no ill'

explanation.surface: A church is accused by a woman of wicked deeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charged by' suggests an accusation, but means CE is filled with HEN then ILL.
explanation.definitionFit: Chenille is a tufted velvety yarn or the fabric woven from it.

clue.text: Smoker new among old Basque separatists

indicators.note: among means placed inside, so the letter for new sits within the group

parts.note: ETA was the Basque separatist group, disbanded in 2018

explanation.surface: A fresh cigarette lit among veteran Basque militants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoker' looks like a person with a cigarette, but it is a smoking volcano.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is an active volcano in Sicily, a mountain that smokes.

clue.text: Dish a man chews is one of ham sandwiches

definitions.text: Dish a man chews is one of ham sandwiches

parts.words: Dish a man chews is one of ham sandwiches
parts.note: the letters of 'dish a man chews' are exactly the letters of 'ham sandwiches' rearranged, so the clue's first phrase is one of these word puzzles

explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes itself: 'Dish a man chews' uses the letters of 'ham sandwiches' in a new order, so it is one.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase made by rearranging the letters of another is exactly this kind of word puzzle.

clue.text: Satirical artist in house with courtyard

parts.note: a garth is an enclosed courtyard, especially a cloister garden

explanation.surface: A satirical painter lives in a house with a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: William Hogarth was the eighteenth-century English painter and engraver of satirical scenes.

clue.text: Vatican report altogether groundless?

indicators.note: report means as heard, so the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: altogether means wholly, and the sea is somewhere with no ground underfoot

explanation.surface: A story about the Vatican that has no basis whatever.
explanation.walkthrough: WHOLLY (altogether) plus SEA (groundless: no land) said out loud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy See is the papal government seated in the Vatican, often used as its synonym.

clue.text: President right into smoked mutton

indicators.note: into means put inside, so the letter for right goes into the meat word

parts.note: macon is mutton cured and smoked like bacon

explanation.surface: The president tucks right into some smoked mutton.
explanation.walkthrough: MACON is a wartime British bacon substitute made from mutton.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel Macron is the French head of state, a president.

clue.text: Belt held right over trousers

indicators.note: over in a down clue signals reading the letters upwards, back to front
trousers as a verb means pockets or holds, so the letters are tucked inside the words

explanation.surface: A belt keeps one's trousers held up properly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' is a verb: 'held right' holds ELDRIG, which 'over' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A girdle is a belt or sash worn round the waist.

clue.text: Tooth decay shows no initial sign

indicators.note: no initial means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: caries is the dental term for tooth decay

explanation.surface: The dentist sees no early signs of rot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' looks like a symptom, but it is a sign of the zodiac.
explanation.definitionFit: Aries, the ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

clue.text: Departs from Durham town for cemetery

indicators.note: from here means taken away from, so the letter leaves the town name

parts.note: Darlington is a town in County Durham, north-east England
D is the abbreviation for departs on timetables

explanation.surface: Trains leaving a northern town on the way to a graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: Darlington is a town in County Durham in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia is the famous US military burial ground.

clue.text: Line excised from standard opera

indicators.note: excised from means cut out of, so the letter is removed

parts.note: normal means standard, ordinary

explanation.surface: A line has been cut from a standard opera score.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is Bellini's 1831 opera about a druid priestess.

clue.text: Maoists argued about blocking road south

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the way, so the shuffled letters are placed inside the road abbreviation
about signals the letters of argued are rearranged

explanation.surface: Protesters argue while blocking the road south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' shuffles 'argued' to EDGUAR and 'blocking' sets it within the road; 'argued about' reads as a dispute but is the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Guards were the student militia of Mao's Cultural Revolution in China.

clue.text: Country sport — run length around area

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the area letter sits between the other two

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A country sport involving a run around the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' is an adjective here, as in country life.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural means relating to the countryside, as country does used adjectivally.

clue.text: Born in Cambridge alongside Backs

indicators.note: backs means the rear ends, so the final letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: Born in a Cambridge college beside the river lawns.
explanation.walkthrough: The Backs is a stretch of Cambridge where colleges back onto the river; here 'Backs' signals the last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Née, French for born, marks a woman's maiden name.

clue.text: Woman captivating fellow in the flesh?

definitions.text: Woman captivating fellow in the flesh?

indicators.note: captivating means holding captive, so the woman's word surrounds the rest

parts.note: a female is a woman

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the fellow's letter goes into the meat

parts.note: meat is flesh

explanation.surface: A seductress charming a man in person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivating' and 'in' are both containers; the whole clue also describes the answer, with 'in the flesh' teasing a physical allure.
explanation.definitionFit: A seductive woman who ensnares men is a classic temptress.
